title: The intro is four beats, 25.5 s: four labelled wireframes, one breach pouring, the hull through a topped-up horde, the gunship on a horde in frame
context: The owner watched the twelve-shot showcase (2026-09-19-showcase-built) and cut it to four beats (2026-09-24-intro-simplified): A the key elements as labelled wireframes, B one breach with the swarm coming out, C the tank ramming fifty, D the gunship firing on the enemies below. The three known misses had to go with it: the gunship framed the base, not the breach; nothing from a seat's HUD but the beat's own card; SOL-82's round scope gone, since SOL-82 is now only a wireframe.
outcome: Built. THE TABLE (src/content/showcase.js) is four beats, 25.5 s: elements-wireframe 7 s, breach-swarm 5.5 s, tank-ram 7 s, gunship-guns 6 s, then Isao's ARE YOU READY? unchanged. BEAT A is an element REEL inside one beat: SHOWCASE_ELEMENTS names four subjects (MORK, KORP/GS01, SOL-82, ROTOR sentry), each 1.75 s on the briefing's wireframe stage with its own card and labels. src/fx/wireframe-stage.js gained the labelled treatment: it FITS the camera to the loaded model's bounding box (a 5 m sentry and a 52 m satellite both fill the frame) and reports each label's anchor in canvas pixels; the rail owns the label boxes and leader lines. Anchors are BOX-relative (-1..1 per axis), not node names, so a label lands on the structure it names in every model. BEAT B is the real dive placement 4 cells up and 5 back over the hole, tremor, and the swarm fed on the rail's beat. BEAT C places the hull on open ground beside the breach, drops bodies ROUND THE HULL as it drives (guard-path spawns), re-places it and re-snaps the chase camera every 0.6 s; the ram readout is the one piece of HUD let through the montage's body class, and the still shows '+11 kg x220' over the bodies. BEAT D snaps the gunship's ground track over the breach (new hook `track`), drops 40 bodies under the belly and aims the SEAT itself (yaw 0, pitch -1.5): the gunner's aim is a yaw and pitch relative to the platform, and a seat opened on a page that has taken no seat looks at the HORIZON, where the optic's ray never strikes the ground and the guns fire nothing. SOL-82 never comes online, so its scope cannot appear. DELETED with the shots they served: the showcase hooks `orbit`, `prep`, `seat`, `launch`, `shell`, `nuke`, `laser`, `laserHold`, `laserCam`, `laserLeave` and the beam/seeker/nuke counters; the `.shout` card treatment (TOO MANY ENEMIES! is gone); the old `tank-wireframe`, `gunship-nuke`, `nuke-ground`, `quiver-pov`, `rotor-pov`, `too-many`, `laser-wireframe`, `laser-orbit`, `laser-ground` cases. src/td-tab.js is unchanged at its 13,505-line budget.
alternatives: Holding the montage's first frame until the world is up, as the twelve-shot cut did: the breach needs about a minute to warm and finish opening in the harness, the 25 s ceiling fired first, and the beats then ran with a full spawn queue that released 294 bodies in one frame at 19.5 s. Beat A needs no world at all, so it now IS the loading screen and the wait moved to the cut out of it (60 s ceiling).

Placing the tank on a body every 0.22 s to ram: 30 placements, no ram. A ram is the hull MOVING into a body, and re-placing it resets its lane every frame. The placement is on a 0.6 s metronome, and the camera is snapped AFTER the hull is moved, never before — snapping first photographed the empty base while the hull rammed off screen.

Ramming the first rammable body in the list: it is a guard on the far side of the map, or one still climbing out of the rock with no contact to make, or standing on rock the hull may not enter. ramNext now takes the LAST body that has finished emerging on ground the hull can stand on.

Feeding beats C and D through the breach: a sector closes its breach part way through the montage and a closed one never opens again, so the queue simply grew. Both beats now drop their own bodies through the guard spawn path, which carries its own spawn point and is released the moment it is asked for.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --showcase: PASS on all four beats and all four page-level steps; one screenshot per beat at its midpoint in artifacts/browser/showcase-*.png.

Measured proof from that run: 4 labels on the wireframe at beat A's midpoint (SOL-82: TRACKING WING / APERTURE / RADIATOR VANE), 62 bodies emerging during breach-swarm, 282 rams and combo x282 during tank-ram, +99 gunship round impacts with 113 rammable bodies under the belly during gunship-guns.

Looked at the four stills: A reads as the briefing treatment; B is the hole with the tremor cracks and the mass in it; C is bodies round the frame with the combo readout over them; D is the thermal belly view with the horde under the rings and rounds landing among them.

The --showcase step now asserts the four beats by name, labels present at the reveal, >= 30 emerging, >= 20 rams (the larger of rams and tank kills, never their sum: a ram IS a tank kill), >= 8 gunship impacts and >= 20 bodies in both world hordes.
npm test (121 programs), npm run check (architecture guard: src/td-tab.js at its 13,505 budget, unchanged), and the browser steps --grow, --skip-tutorial, --story-world and --nav green.

Still not read in the stills: the hull itself is not in frame during beat C — the game's own chase camera sits high behind it and looks a cell and a half ahead, so the bodies, the splats and the combo carry the beat and the tank does not.
